title: Chapter Two: What the Guild Keeps

blocks.c: Chapter Two: What the Guild Keeps

The guildhall at Weatherbell kept three things: oil, ledgers, and grudges. The oil was in the cellar, the ledgers were on the long shelf, and the grudges were distributed evenly among the staff so that no one person had to carry more than her share.

Ines went to the ledgers before she went to anyone who might have an opinion about her going to the ledgers. The relevant volume was bound in grey cloth and smelled of the cellar, and its columns had been ruled by someone with more patience than Ines expected ever to have.
Each lamp in the district had a line. Each line carried four marks:

items: the night it was last lit, in the lighter's own hand
the measure of oil drawn for it
the initials of whoever signed the oil out
a small circle, meaning nothing, which everyone agreed was important

blocks.c: The line for the lamp at the end of the lane was full. Every night accounted for, all eleven of them, in a hand that sloped left and pressed hard enough to emboss the page beneath. Oil drawn each evening. Initials signed each evening. Eleven small circles, drawn carefully, as though by someone who had been told they mattered and had not been told why.
Ines put her thumb on the last entry and found the ink still faintly tacky, which is a thing ink stops being after a day and had no business being after eleven.
"You're touching the book," said the archivist, from the doorway, without heat.
"Someone's been lighting a lamp that isn't lit," said Ines.
The archivist came the rest of the way in and shut the door behind her, which was answer enough for the moment.
